summary: William Woodville Rockhill was a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1884).

William Wright was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He taught Arabic at University College London (1855–1856) and Trinity College Dublin (1856–1861), served as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1861–1870), and was Adams Professor at Cambridge (1870–1889).

Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who completed his PhD (1904–1908) under Hermann Jacobi and his Habilitation (~1908–1920) at the University of Bonn. He served as librarian at Bonn's university library (1911–1921) before succeeding Jacobi as Bonn's professor in 1922.

Sinologist Wilt L. Idema earned his degrees at Leiden University, completing his doctorate under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (~1968–1974). He served as professor at Leiden (1976–1999) and later became Professor of Chinese Literature at Harvard University in 2000.
Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan earned her BA at Cornell, followed by a JD and PhD from the University of Chicago. Her faculty posts include Washington and Lee University, the University of Chicago, and the University at Buffalo.
Winston Kyan is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Wu Hung (attested 2006).

Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. Educated primarily at Columbia University, he spent his career there as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies from 1953 to 2017 and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies (1969–1970).

Sinologist and historian Wolfgang Franke studied at the University of Hamburg and Humboldt University of Berlin. After posts at Sichuan and Peking universities in the 1940s, he held the Sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977), succeeding Otto Franke.

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena. He held academic posts at the universities of Greifswald and Jena, and was Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

Wolfgang Schamoni is a Japanologist who studied at Waseda University and earned his doctorate at the University of Bonn (~1968–1974). He held posts at the universities of Munich and Marburg before serving as professor at Heidelberg University from 1985 to 2006.

Philosopher Wolfgang Schultz earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (1899–1904). He served as an administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Wolfram Eberhard worked in Sinology and history. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Seminar for Oriental Languages, taught in China and at Ankara University (1937–1948), and served as Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

Wu Hung is an art historian and Sinologist who studied at CAFA and Harvard. He taught at Harvard before joining the University of Chicago in 1994 as Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History.
Wulstan Fletcher is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xianda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at The University of Hong Kong, studying under K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo (attested 2016).

Xiangguang Zhou worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied under Swami Sivananda Saraswati and served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Allahabad, Lecturer in History at Delhi, and Chancellor at Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua University and earned his PhD under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg at Göttingen. He served for decades at Peking University, becoming a professor in 1946 and later Life Professor.
